title: A Sacred Oath
synopsis: Emperor Liu Zhi tries to reclaim power from the imperial in-laws.

fullText.simplified:
歃血为盟

    做皇帝容易吗？这个答案，我们并不知道，毕竟，我们都没有做过皇帝。但是，从东汉的历史来看，皇帝有可能是一种“高危”的职业。
    从刘庄的孙子当上皇帝开始，很长一段时间，国家的权力都落到了外戚手上。外戚也就是皇帝的妻子、母亲的家族。
    自古以来，如果皇帝娶了身份尊贵的妻子，往往可以得到她家族的帮助。东汉一共有十二个皇帝，其中就有七位都是依靠外戚才顺利当上皇帝的。这七位皇帝中，有一位才出生不到一百天就当上了皇帝，不到一年就逝世了。另一位一岁当皇帝，三岁就逝世了。
    外戚当权，弊端远远大于益处。这些小皇帝做什么事都只能听外戚的。久而久之，大家就只知道外戚，不知道皇帝了。比如外戚梁将军，当时权倾朝野，所有的人都要听他的，他想让谁当皇帝，谁就可以当皇帝。有一个小皇帝，因为指责他“肆无忌惮”，就被他下毒杀死了。然后，这位梁将军把东汉第十一位皇帝刘志送上了皇位。那时候，刘志才十五岁，完全不是梁将军的对手。但梁将军这次看走眼了，这个小皇帝还真把权力从外戚手中抢了回来。
    要知道，外戚们有着比皇帝更高的地位。基本上，所有的大臣都投靠了外戚，而不听从皇帝。刘志能怎么办呢？他只能把眼光投向了身边的下人——宦官。
    为了不被梁将军发觉，刘志躲在厕所里，和他的五个宦官说了自己的情况。他们小心翼翼，每个人把自己的血放进一碗酒里，然后每人喝了一口，说：“现在，我的身体里有你的血，你的身体里有我的血，我们就是兄弟了！如果失败，我们就一起死！”
    很难相信，皇帝会和下人做“兄弟”，但这件事就这样发生了。刘志如此不择手段，死都不怕，只想打败外戚。
    按理说，一个没有权力的皇帝，与五个普普通通的宦官合伙，是不可能赢过手握大权的梁将军的。但是，梁将军或许是太轻敌了，没把皇帝放在眼里。这天，五个宦官叫上了一群人，冲到了梁家，包围了他们。哪怕梁将军有再大的本事，这一刻他只能认输。就这样，他自杀了。
    从那以后，刘志终于从外戚的威胁中脱离出来，不用天天担心被外戚杀死了。那五个宦官也因此获得了无上的地位。
    宦官们的身体不健全，没有孩子，于是他们就拼命要钱，毫无节制。譬如，他们把官位卖给别人，又大肆欺负百姓，抢走百姓的地等等。有人举报他们，但刘志并没有处罚这些宦官。因为在他心中，这些永远没有孩子的宦官，才会永远听他的话。宦官比外戚好太多了！
    等到第十二位皇帝上位，他也相信自己的宦官们，称他们为“爸爸”、“妈妈”，宦官的势力就更大了。外戚们不服气，心想：“凭什么宦官能有权力，我却不能？”这两帮人你争我抢，致使国家越来越乱。
    百姓们在这样的环境中，过着痛苦的生活。有一天，他们再也忍受不了了，就在脑袋上缠一块黄布，称自己为“黄巾军”，开始造反了！
    “黄巾军”声势不小，无法遏制，国家的军队一次又一次地被打败了。这时候，外戚和宦官们也害怕了。他们想：“如果我们打不过，那总有人打得过。”于是，他们想了一个办法，把权力分给各个地方的大官，让他们去对付黄巾军。
    不得不说，这真是个糟透了的办法。当这些遍布全国的大官可以自己拥有军队，可以自己打仗，那皇帝还有什么权力呢？
    果不其然，各个地方的大官们打败了黄巾军后，这些大官们也就变成了许多个无名的“皇帝”。他们谁也不听别人的话，都想自己成为真正的皇帝。
    其中有一个叫董卓的人最厉害。他带着兵打进了都城，打败了宦官和外戚，控制了九岁的小皇帝。有了皇帝作为人质，董卓就可以命令全天下的人了。但其他人也很不服气，都不想听董卓的话，有的人决定攻打董卓，恢复汉室；有的人趁乱到处出兵，想自己当皇帝。    就这样，一个新的时代——三国时代到来了，无数个有血有肉的英雄出现在世人面前。

sentences.traditional: 他們小心翼翼，每個人把自己的血放進一碗酒裡，然後每人喝了一口，說：
sentences.pinyin: tā men xiǎo xīn yì yì měi ge rén bǎ zì jǐ de xiě fàng jìn yì wǎn jiǔ lǐ rán hòu měi rén hē le yì kǒu shuō
sentences.english: In order not to be discovered by General Liang, Liu Zhi hid in the toilet and talked to his five eunuchs about his situation.

sentences.simplified: “现在，我的身体里有你的血，你的身体里有我的血，
sentences.traditional: “現在，我的身體裡有你的血，你的身體裡有我的血，
sentences.pinyin: xiàn zài wǒ de shēn tǐ lǐ yǒu nǐ de xiě nǐ de shēn tǐ lǐ yǒu wǒ de xiě
sentences.english: With great care, each of them put some blood into a bowl of wine, then they all took a sip and said, ..

sentences.simplified: 我们就是兄弟了！如果失败，我们就一起死！”
sentences.traditional: 我們就是兄弟了！如果失敗，我們就一起死！”
sentences.pinyin: wǒ men jiù shì xiōng dì le rú guǒ shī bài wǒ men jiù yì qǐ sǐ
sentences.english: .. “Now I have your blood in my body, and you have my blood in your body.
We are brothers! If we fail, we will die together!”

sentences.simplified: 很难相信，皇帝会和下人做“兄弟”，但这件事就这样发生了。
sentences.traditional: 很難相信，皇帝會和下人做“兄弟”，但這件事就這樣發生了。
sentences.pinyin: hěn nán xiāng xìn huáng dì huì hé xià rén zuò xiōng dì dàn zhè jiàn shì jiù zhè yàng fā shēng le

sentences.simplified: 刘志如此不择手段，死都不怕，只想打败外戚。
sentences.traditional: 劉志如此不擇手段，死都不怕，只想打敗外戚。
sentences.pinyin: liú zhì rú cǐ bù zé shǒu duàn sǐ dōu bú pà zhǐ xiǎng dǎ bài wài qī
sentences.english: It’s hard to believe that the emperor would be “brothers” with his servants, but this is how it happened.
Liu Zhi would stop at nothing and wasn’t afraid of death. He just wanted to defeat the imperial in-laws.

sentences.simplified: 按理说，一个没有权力的皇帝，与五个普普通通的宦官合伙，
sentences.traditional: 按理說，一個沒有權力的皇帝，與五個普普通通的宦官合伙，
sentences.pinyin: àn lǐ shuō yí ge méi yǒu quán lì de huáng dì yǔ wǔ ge pǔ pǔ tōng tōng de huàn guān hé huǒ

sentences.simplified: 是不可能赢过手握大权的梁将军的。
sentences.traditional: 是不可能贏過手握大權的梁將軍的。
sentences.pinyin: shì bù kě néng yíng guò shǒu wò dà quán de liáng jiāng jūn de
sentences.english: In the ordinary course of events, an emperor without power, acting jointly with five ordinary eunuchs, ..

sentences.simplified: 但是，梁将军或许是太轻敌了，没把皇帝放在眼里。
sentences.traditional: 但是，梁將軍或許是太輕敵了，沒把皇帝放在眼裡。
sentences.pinyin: dàn shì liáng jiāng jūn huò xǔ shì tài qīng dí le méi bǎ huáng dì fàng zài yǎn lǐ
sentences.english: .. would be unable to win against the powerful General Liang.

sentences.simplified: 这天，五个宦官叫上了一群人，冲到了梁家，包围了他们。
sentences.traditional: 這天，五個宦官叫上了一群人，衝到了梁家，包圍了他們。
sentences.pinyin: zhè tiān wǔ ge huàn guān jiào shàng le yì qún rén chōng dào le liáng jiā bāo wéi le tā men
sentences.english: However, General Liang perhaps underestimated the enemy too much and did not take the emperor seriously.

sentences.simplified: 哪怕梁将军有再大的本事，这一刻他只能认输。就这样，他自杀了。
sentences.traditional: 哪怕梁將軍有再大的本事，這一刻他只能認輸。就這樣，他自殺了。
sentences.pinyin: nǎ pà liáng jiāng jūn yǒu zài dà de běn shi zhè yí kè tā zhǐ néng rèn shū jiù zhè yàng tā zì shā le
sentences.english: On that day, the five eunuchs rallied a group of people, rushed to the Liang family home, and surrounded them.
Even though General Liang had great skill, this time, he could only admit defeat. So, he committed suicide.

sentences.simplified: 从那以后，刘志终于从外戚的威胁中脱离出来，
sentences.traditional: 從那以後，劉志終於從外戚的威脅中脫離出來，
sentences.pinyin: cóng nà yǐ hòu liú zhì zhōng yú cóng wài qī de wēi xié zhōng tuō lí chu lai

sentences.simplified: 不用天天担心被外戚杀死了。
sentences.traditional: 不用天天擔心被外戚殺死了。
sentences.pinyin: bú yòng tiān tiān dān xīn bèi wài qī shā sǐ le
sentences.english: From that moment on, Liu Zhi was finally free from the threat of the imperial in-laws, ..

sentences.simplified: 那五个宦官也因此获得了无上的地位。
sentences.traditional: 那五個宦官也因此獲得了無上的地位。
sentences.pinyin: nà wǔ ge huàn guān yě yīn cǐ huò dé le wú shàng de dì wèi
sentences.english: .. and did not have to worry about being killed by them every day.
As a result, those five eunuchs were given supreme status.

sentences.simplified: 宦官们的身体不健全，没有孩子，于是他们就拼命要钱，毫无节制。
sentences.traditional: 宦官們的身體不健全，沒有孩子，於是他們就拼命要錢，毫無節制。
sentences.pinyin: huàn guān men de shēn tǐ bú jiàn quán méi yǒu hái zi yú shì tā men jiù pīn mìng yào qián háo wú jié zhì

sentences.simplified: 譬如，他们把官位卖给别人，又大肆欺负百姓，抢走百姓的地等等。
sentences.traditional: 譬如，他們把官位賣給別人，又大肆欺負百姓，搶走百姓的地等等。
sentences.pinyin: pì rú tā men bǎ guān wèi mài gěi bié ren yòu dà sì qī fu bǎi xìng qiǎng zǒu bǎi xìng de dì děng děng
sentences.english: Due to their condition, eunuchs did not have children, so they demanded money from everyone, completely without restraint.

sentences.simplified: 有人举报他们，但刘志并没有处罚这些宦官。
sentences.traditional: 有人舉報他們，但劉志並沒有處罰這些宦官。
sentences.pinyin: yǒu rén jǔ bào tā men dàn liú zhì bìng méi yǒu chǔ fá zhè xiē huàn guān
sentences.english: For example, they sold official positions to others, bullied ordinary people without restraint, and took away the land of ordinary people.

sentences.simplified: 因为在他心中，这些永远没有孩子的宦官，才会永远听他的话。
sentences.traditional: 因為在他心中，這些永遠沒有孩子的宦官，才會永遠聽他的話。
sentences.pinyin: yīn wèi zài tā xīn zhōng zhè xiē yǒng yuǎn méi yǒu hái zi de huàn guān cái huì yǒng yuǎn tīng tā de huà
sentences.english: Some people reported them, but Liu Zhi did not punish these eunuchs.

sentences.simplified: 宦官比外戚好太多了！
sentences.traditional: 宦官比外戚好太多了！
sentences.pinyin: huàn guān bǐ wài qī hǎo tài duō le
sentences.english: Because in his mind, these eunuchs, who would never have children, would always do as he said.
Eunuchs were so much better than imperial in-laws!

sentences.simplified: 等到第十二位皇帝上位，他也相信自己的宦官们，
sentences.traditional: 等到第十二位皇帝上位，他也相信自己的宦官們，
sentences.pinyin: děng dào dì shí èr wèi huáng dì shàng wèi tā yě xiāng xìn zì jǐ de huàn guān men

sentences.simplified: 称他们为“爸爸”、“妈妈”，宦官的势力就更大了。
sentences.traditional: 稱他們為“爸爸”、“媽媽”，宦官的勢力就更大了。
sentences.pinyin: chēng tā men wéi bà ba mā ma huàn guān de shì li jiù gèng dà le
sentences.english: When the twelfth emperor came to the throne, he also trusted his eunuchs.

sentences.simplified: 外戚们不服气，心想：“凭什么宦官能有权力，我却不能？”
sentences.traditional: 外戚們不服氣，心想：“憑什麼宦官能有權力，我卻不能？”
sentences.pinyin: wài qī men bù fú qì xīn xiǎng píng shén me huàn guān néng yǒu quán lì wǒ què bù néng
sentences.english: He called them “Dad” and “Mom”, and the power of the eunuchs became even greater.

sentences.simplified: 这两帮人你争我抢，致使国家越来越乱。
sentences.traditional: 這兩幫人你爭我搶，致使國家越來越亂。
sentences.pinyin: zhè liǎng bāng rén nǐ zhēng wǒ qiǎng zhì shǐ guó jiā yuè lái yuè luàn
sentences.english: The imperial in-laws didn’t accept this and thought, “Why should the eunuchs have power, but I can’t?”
These two groups were competing fiercely against each other, causing the country to become more and more chaotic.

sentences.simplified: 百姓们在这样的环境中，过着痛苦的生活。
sentences.traditional: 百姓們在這樣的環境中，過著痛苦的生活。
sentences.pinyin: bǎi xìng men zài zhè yàng de huán jìng zhōng guò zhe tòng kǔ de shēng huó

sentences.simplified: 有一天，他们再也忍受不了了，
sentences.traditional: 有一天，他們再也忍受不了了，
sentences.pinyin: yǒu yì tiān tā men zài yě rěn shòu bù liǎo le
sentences.english: In this environment, ordinary people lived in misery.

sentences.simplified: 就在脑袋上缠一块黄布，称自己为“黄巾军”，开始造反了！
sentences.traditional: 就在腦袋上纏一塊黃布，稱自己為“黃巾軍”，開始造反了！
sentences.pinyin: jiù zài nǎo dài shang chán yí kuài huáng bù chēng zì jǐ wéi huáng jīn jūn kāi shǐ zào fǎn le
sentences.english: One day, they could not stand it anymore.
They wrapped a piece of yellow cloth around their heads, called themselves the “Yellow Turban Army”, and started a rebellion!

sentences.simplified: “黄巾军”声势不小，无法遏制，国家的军队一次又一次地被打败了。
sentences.traditional: “黃巾軍”聲勢不小，無法遏制，國家的軍隊一次又一次地被打敗了。
sentences.pinyin: huáng jīn jūn shēng shì bù xiǎo wú fǎ è zhì guó jiā de jūn duì yí cì yòu yí cì de bèi dǎ bài le

sentences.simplified: 这时候，外戚和宦官们也害怕了。
sentences.traditional: 這時候，外戚和宦官們也害怕了。
sentences.pinyin: zhè shí hou wài qī hé huàn guān men yě hài pà le
sentences.english: The “Yellow Turban Army” was too powerful to be contained, and the country’s troops were defeated again and again.

sentences.simplified: 他们想：“如果我们打不过，那总有人打得过。”
sentences.traditional: 他們想：“如果我們打不過，那總有人打得過。”
sentences.pinyin: tā men xiǎng rú guǒ wǒ men dǎ bú guò nà zǒng yǒu rén dǎ de guò
sentences.english: This time, the imperial in-laws and eunuchs were also afraid.

sentences.simplified: 于是，他们想了一个办法，把权力分给各个地方的大官，
sentences.traditional: 於是，他們想了一個辦法，把權力分給各個地方的大官，
sentences.pinyin: yú shì tā men xiǎng le yí ge bàn fǎ bǎ quán lì fēn gěi gè gè dì fang de dà guān
sentences.english: They thought, “If we can’t beat them, then someone else can do it.”

sentences.simplified: 让他们去对付黄巾军。
sentences.traditional: 讓他們去對付黃巾軍。
sentences.pinyin: ràng tā men qù duì fu huáng jīn jūn
sentences.english: So, they came up with the idea to divide power between major officials from each locality, ..
.. and let them deal with the Yellow Turban Army.

sentences.simplified: 不得不说，这真是个糟透了的办法。
sentences.traditional: 不得不說，這真是個糟透了的辦法。
sentences.pinyin: bù dé bù shuō zhè zhēn shì ge zāo tòu le de bàn fǎ

sentences.simplified: 当这些遍布全国的大官可以自己拥有军队，
sentences.traditional: 當這些遍布全國的大官可以自己擁有軍隊，
sentences.pinyin: dāng zhè xiē biàn bù quán guó de dà guān kě yǐ zì jǐ yōng yǒu jūn duì
sentences.english: Needless to say, this was a really bad idea.

sentences.simplified: 可以自己打仗，那皇帝还有什么权力呢？
sentences.traditional: 可以自己打仗，那皇帝還有什麼權力呢？
sentences.pinyin: kě yǐ zì jǐ dǎ zhàng nà huáng dì hái yǒu shén me quán lì ne
sentences.english: As these important officials spread throughout the country could have their own armies ..
.. and could fight their own battles, then what power did the emperor have?

sentences.simplified: 果不其然，各个地方的大官们打败了黄巾军后，
sentences.traditional: 果不其然，各個地方的大官們打敗了黃巾軍後，
sentences.pinyin: guǒ bù qí rán gè gè dì fang de dà guān men dǎ bài le huáng jīn jūn hòu

sentences.simplified: 这些大官们也就变成了许多个无名的“皇帝”。
sentences.traditional: 這些大官們也就變成了許多個無名的“皇帝”。
sentences.pinyin: zhè xiē dà guān men yě jiù biàn chéng le xǔ duō ge wú míng de huáng dì
sentences.english: Just as expected, after the local officials defeated the Yellow Turban Army, ..

sentences.simplified: 他们谁也不听别人的话，都想自己成为真正的皇帝。
sentences.traditional: 他們誰也不聽別人的話，都想自己成為真正的皇帝。
sentences.pinyin: tā men shéi yě bù tīng bié ren de huà dōu xiǎng zì jǐ chéng wéi zhēn zhèng de huáng dì
sentences.english: .. these important officials also turned into many “emperors” in all but name.
None of them listened to anyone else, and they all wanted to become the real emperor themselves.

sentences.simplified: 其中有一个叫董卓的人最厉害。
sentences.traditional: 其中有一個叫董卓的人最厲害。
sentences.pinyin: qí zhōng yǒu yí ge jiào dǒng zhuó de rén zuì lì hai

sentences.simplified: 他带着兵打进了都城，打败了宦官和外戚，控制了九岁的小皇帝。
sentences.traditional: 他帶著兵打進了都城，打敗了宦官和外戚，控制了九歲的小皇帝。
sentences.pinyin: tā dài zhe bīng dǎ jìn le dū chéng dǎ bài le huàn guān hé wài qī kòng zhì le jiǔ suì de xiǎo huáng dì
sentences.english: The most powerful among them was called Dong Zhuo.

sentences.simplified: 有了皇帝作为人质，董卓就可以命令全天下的人了。
sentences.traditional: 有了皇帝作為人質，董卓就可以命令全天下的人了。
sentences.pinyin: yǒu le huáng dì zuò wéi rén zhì dǒng zhuó jiù kě yǐ mìng lìng quán tiān xià de rén le
sentences.english: He led his troops into the capital, defeated the eunuchs and imperial in-laws, and took control of the young 9-year-old emperor.

sentences.simplified: 但其他人也很不服气，都不想听董卓的话，
sentences.traditional: 但其他人也很不服氣，都不想聽董卓的話，
sentences.pinyin: dàn qí tā rén yě hěn bù fú qì dōu bù xiǎng tīng dǒng zhuó de huà
sentences.english: With the emperor as a hostage, Dong Zhuo could command the people under heaven.

sentences.simplified: 有的人决定攻打董卓，恢复汉室；
sentences.traditional: 有的人決定攻打董卓，恢復漢室；
sentences.pinyin: yǒu de rén jué dìng gōng dǎ dǒng zhuó huī fù hàn shì
sentences.english: But other people did not submit. They did not want to obey Dong Zhuo.

sentences.simplified: 有的人趁乱到处出兵，想自己当皇帝。
sentences.traditional: 有的人趁亂到處出兵，想自己當皇帝。
sentences.pinyin: yǒu de rén chèn luàn dào chù chū bīng xiǎng zì jǐ dāng huáng dì
sentences.english: Some of them decided to attack Dong Zhuo and restore the Han Dynasty.
Others took advantage of the chaos and sent troops everywhere. They wanted to become emperor themselves.

sentences.simplified: 就这样，一个新的时代——三国时代到来了，无数个有血有肉的英雄出现在世人面前。
sentences.traditional: 就這樣，一個新的時代——三國時代到來了，無數個有血有肉的英雄出現在世人面前。
sentences.pinyin: jiù zhè yàng yí ge xīn de shí dài sān guó shí dài dào lái le wú shù ge yǒu xiě yǒu ròu de yīng xióng chū xiàn zài shì rén miàn qián

sentence_translations: A Sacred Oath
Was it easy to be an emperor? We can’t know the answer to that. After all, none of us have ever been an emperor.
However, based on the history of the Eastern Han Dynasty, emperor might have been a “high-risk” occupation.
Starting from the time Liu Zhuang’s grandson became emperor, ..
.. the power of the state fell into the hands of the imperial in-laws for a long period.
The imperial in-laws were the family of the emperor’s wife or mother.
Since ancient times, if the emperor married a wife of high status, he could often get help from her family.
There were 12 emperors during the Eastern Han Dynasty, and 7 of them relied on imperial in-laws to become emperors.
One of these seven emperors was born less than 100 days before he became emperor and died in less than a year.
Another one became emperor at the age of one and died at the age of three.
The disadvantages of having imperial in-laws in power far outweighed the benefits.
These young emperors could only do what their imperial in-laws told them to in everything they did.
Over time, everyone only knew of the imperial in-laws, not the emperor.
For example, the imperial in-law General Liang was so powerful that he controlled the imperial court and the ordinary people.
Everyone had to obey him, and he could make whoever he wanted emperor.
He poisoned a young emperor to death because the young emperor denounced him as “completely unscrupulous”.
Then, this General Liang put Liu Zhi, the eleventh emperor of the Eastern Han Dynasty, on the throne.
At that time, Liu Zhi was only 15 years old and was no match against General Liang.
But this time General Liang made an error of judgment. This little emperor really snatched power back from his imperial in-laws.
It is important to know that the imperial in-laws had a higher status than the emperor.
Basically, all the ministers sought the patronage of the imperial in-laws instead of obeying the emperor.
What could Liu Zhi do? He had no choice but to turn his eyes to the servants around him—the eunuchs.
In order not to be discovered by General Liang, Liu Zhi hid in the toilet and talked to his five eunuchs about his situation.
With great care, each of them put some blood into a bowl of wine, then they all took a sip and said, ..
.. “Now I have your blood in my body, and you have my blood in your body.
We are brothers! If we fail, we will die together!”
It’s hard to believe that the emperor would be “brothers” with his servants, but this is how it happened.
Liu Zhi would stop at nothing and wasn’t afraid of death. He just wanted to defeat the imperial in-laws.
In the ordinary course of events, an emperor without power, acting jointly with five ordinary eunuchs, ..
.. would be unable to win against the powerful General Liang.
However, General Liang perhaps underestimated the enemy too much and did not take the emperor seriously.
On that day, the five eunuchs rallied a group of people, rushed to the Liang family home, and surrounded them.
Even though General Liang had great skill, this time, he could only admit defeat. So, he committed suicide.
From that moment on, Liu Zhi was finally free from the threat of the imperial in-laws, ..
.. and did not have to worry about being killed by them every day.
As a result, those five eunuchs were given supreme status.
Due to their condition, eunuchs did not have children, so they demanded money from everyone, completely without restraint.
For example, they sold official positions to others, bullied ordinary people without restraint, and took away the land of ordinary people.
Some people reported them, but Liu Zhi did not punish these eunuchs.
Because in his mind, these eunuchs, who would never have children, would always do as he said.
Eunuchs were so much better than imperial in-laws!
When the twelfth emperor came to the throne, he also trusted his eunuchs.
He called them “Dad” and “Mom”, and the power of the eunuchs became even greater.
The imperial in-laws didn’t accept this and thought, “Why should the eunuchs have power, but I can’t?”
These two groups were competing fiercely against each other, causing the country to become more and more chaotic.
In this environment, ordinary people lived in misery.
One day, they could not stand it anymore.
They wrapped a piece of yellow cloth around their heads, called themselves the “Yellow Turban Army”, and started a rebellion!
The “Yellow Turban Army” was too powerful to be contained, and the country’s troops were defeated again and again.
This time, the imperial in-laws and eunuchs were also afraid.
They thought, “If we can’t beat them, then someone else can do it.”
So, they came up with the idea to divide power between major officials from each locality, ..
.. and let them deal with the Yellow Turban Army.
Needless to say, this was a really bad idea.
As these important officials spread throughout the country could have their own armies ..
.. and could fight their own battles, then what power did the emperor have?
Just as expected, after the local officials defeated the Yellow Turban Army, ..
.. these important officials also turned into many “emperors” in all but name.
None of them listened to anyone else, and they all wanted to become the real emperor themselves.
The most powerful among them was called Dong Zhuo.
He led his troops into the capital, defeated the eunuchs and imperial in-laws, and took control of the young 9-year-old emperor.
With the emperor as a hostage, Dong Zhuo could command the people under heaven.
But other people did not submit. They did not want to obey Dong Zhuo.
Some of them decided to attack Dong Zhuo and restore the Han Dynasty.
Others took advantage of the chaos and sent troops everywhere. They wanted to become emperor themselves.
In this way, a new era—the Three Kingdoms era—came about. Countless real-life heroes appeared in front of the common people.
